jobs.title: Fitness Programs Manager (USU) at CSUN 10293 - University Student Union
jobs.description: Employer: CSUN 10293 - University Student Union Expires: 12/09/2026 IN ORDER TO BE CONSIDERED FOR THE POSITION, PLEASE SUBMIT YOUR APPLICATION HERE: https://careers.pageuppeople.com/873/nr/en-us/job/564158/fitness-programs-manager-usu ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY STUDENT UNIONThe University Student Union, as the heart of campus, uplifts and empowers students to achieve educational, personal and professional goals by providing leadership development, meaningful employment, and innovative programs, services and facilities. We promote equity, inclusion and well-being, while encouraging social justice advocacy to help Matadors feel heard, respected and connected to CSUN. Our facilities include a University Student Union and a 138,000 square foot Student Recreation Center (SRC). The SRC is a facility for exercise and leisure activity that promotes lifelong health and wellness. ABOUT THE UNIVERSITYOne of the largest universities in the country, California State University, Northridge (CSUN) is an urban, comprehensive university that delivers award-winning undergraduate and graduate programs to nearly 40,000 students annually and counts more than 330,000 alumni who elevate Southern California and beyond. Since its founding in 1958, CSUN has made a significant and long-term economic impact on California, generating nearly $1.9 billion in economic impact and more than 11,700 jobs each year. The LAEDC recognized CSUN as its 2015 Eddy Award winner for its positive economic impact. Serving more students on Pell Grants than any other institution in California, CSUN is also a social elevator and one of the most diverse universities in the country. CSUN ranks 13th in awarding bachelor’s degrees to underrepresented minority students and seventh in bachelor’s degrees to Latino students, serves the 13th largest Jewish student population, and enrolls the largest number of students who are Deaf and hard-of-hearing of any U.S. state university. The journal Nature recently named CSUN a Rising Star for scientific research, and the NSF ranks CSUN in the top five nationally among similar institutions for graduates who go on to earn doctorates in the sciences. CSUN is where individuals rise. And through them, so does Greater Los Angeles and beyond. POSITION SUMMARY:Under the guidance of the Assistant Director, Fitness & Wellness, the Manager, Fitness Programs is responsible for the management and oversight of Student Recreation Center (SRC) Fitness programs and services including group exercise, personal and small group training, and the boxing program. The position supervises a full-time staff employee and part-time non-student employees and indirectly supervises part-time student assistant employees. Responsibilities include program development and assessment, staff development, budget management, implementation of established safety practices, and collaboration with campus and industry partners. The Manager guides continuous improvement of fitness programs and services to provide inclusive, accessible, and high-quality opportunities that support student well-being and engagement and align with the mission of the University Student Union (USU). ESSENTIAL DUTIES:Provide operational leadership and oversight of the development, implementation, and evaluation of SRC Fitness programs and services, including:Group exercisePersonal trainingComplementary services including fitness assessments, equipment orientations, and recovery sessions)Small group trainingBoxingSpecial events, challenges, and campaignsWorkshops and other instructional programmingNon-credit instruction and professional certifications;Supervise, train, and evaluate the work of one (1) full-time Fitness Training Coordinator, one (1) part-time Student Event Assistant, and approximately ten (10) part-time, non-student Group Exercise Instructors including monitoring performance, providing regular feedback, generating performance evaluations, and administering disciplinary action as necessary; Provide indirect supervision to approximately six (6) part-time student assistant employees, including five (5) Student Boxing Fitness Assistants and one (1) Student Boxing Supervisor, and approximately nine (9) part-time non-student Personal Trainers, ensuring consistent standards of safety, service, instruction, and program delivery;Oversee the design, scheduling, implementation, and evaluation of fitness programming that reflects industry trends, member interest, participation data, and program outcomes, ensuring offerings are inclusive, responsive to needs, and accessible to a diverse campus community;Oversee scheduling and operational systems that support SRC Fitness programs and services (e.g., Connect2, MindBody, WhenToWork, Fusion), ensuring staff are appropriately trained in their use; Develop and manage the SRC Fitness department annual operating budget that support programs, services, and operations, including tracking expenditures, forecasting operational and programmatic needs, allocating resources, and providing recommendations regarding equipment replacement, facility improvements, capital needs, and program support to the Assistant Director;Collaborate with USU departments to coordinate, promote, and evaluate SRC Fitness programs and services;Oversee implementation of established risk management and safety practices for SRC Fitness programs and services, including participant safety information, incident and accident reporting, analysis of safety trends, identification of recurring concerns, and implementation of corrective actions within the scope of the position; Ensure staff receive appropriate training, maintain required certifications, and consistently follow established safety procedures;Ensure SRC Fitness programs, services, and instruction comply with applicable professional standards, certification requirements, scope-of-practice guidelines, and USU and SRC policies and procedures;Resolve member and program concerns that remain unresolved by frontline staff or the Coordinator; identify recurring issues and escalate matters requiring further review to the Assistant Director;Develop, implement, evaluate, and recommend revisions to operational policies, procedures, and service guidelines for SRC Fitness programs and services under the direction of the Assistant Director;Coordinate ongoing staff development and training in customer service, operational procedures, conflict resolution, diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility, emergency preparedness, and program-specific practices;Provide recommendations to the Assistant Director regarding program development, operational improvements, service enhancements, and emerging fitness trends to support the continued growth and effectiveness of fitness programs and services;Monitor program participation, revenue, and expenses; recommend pricing and resource allocation adjustments to the Assistant Director to support program needs and financial sustainability;Coordinate scheduling, logistics, equipment use, and facility reservations for SRC Fitness programs, services, and events;Assess and identify operational needs and provide recommendations related to equipment replacement, facility enhancements, resource needs, service delivery, and other operational priorities to the Assistant Director; coordinate implementation of approved priorities with appropriate staff and departments as necessary;Coordinate the recruitment, selection, onboarding, training, and retention of SRC Fitness program staff; assess staffing needs and recommend staffing levels and structure to the Assistant Director;Contribute operational knowledge, assessment findings, and fitness expertise to departmental planning and strategic initiatives under the direction of the Assistant Director;Develop, implement, monitor, and evaluate annual SRC Fitness strategic initiatives and goals aligned with USU, SRC, and departmental priorities; track progress, identify barriers, and provide recommendations to the Assistant Director to support successful completion and continuous improvement;Cultivate and reinforce positive relationships with students, facility, staff, and community members to promote engagement and support student well-being as directed by the Assistant Director;Coordinate and maintain partnerships with campus entities and industry organizations relevant to Fitness programs and services under strategic direction of Assistant Director;Prepare written communications such as monthly reports, annual reports, program statistics, etc.;Actively serve on a variety of SRC, USU, and University committees and work teams, as assigned; Represent the SRC and USU on assigned committees, within professional associations, and at regional and national conferences (e.g. NIRSA, ACUI, HFA), as approved by the Assistant Director;Review and update job descriptions as necessary;Perform other related duties as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS:Education:Equivalent to graduation from a four-year college or university, preferably with a major in Sport Management, Recreation and Tourism Management, Public Health, Kinesiology/Exercise Science, Business Administration, or a related field. Specialized experience during which the applicant has acquired and successfully applied the knowledge and abilities shown above may be substituted for the required education on a year-for-year basis.Experience:Equivalent to three years of professional-level experience administering or managing fitness and/or wellness-based programs and services, including experience instructing group exercise classes and/or providing personal training services within a collegiate recreation, commercial, corporate, municipal, or similar fitness setting.Special Requirements:Must possess a current group exercise and/or personal training certification from a nationally recognized certifying organization (e.g. AFAA, ISSA, ACE, NASM, NSCA, or equivalent).Must possess a current CPR/AED certification or the ability to obtain certification within the first 30 days of employment.Preferred Qualifications:Master’s degree in Kinesiology/Exercise Science, Recreation and Tourism Management, Sport Management, Public Health, Higher Education Administration, Business Administration, or a related field.Supervision experience.Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities:Knowledge of fitness program administration, exercise science, and fitness industry standardsWorking knowledge of employee supervision, training, scheduling, and performance managementKnowledge of risk management, emergency response, safety practices, and mandated reporting requirementsWorking knowledge of budgeting, expenditure monitoring, forecasting, and resource allocationGeneral knowledge of student development, well-being, and engagement in collegiate recreationAbility to develop, implement, market, and evaluate fitness programs and servicesAbility to analyze program, financial, safety, and operational data and recommend improvementsAbility to develop and revise operational policies and procedures and interpret and apply University, USU, and SRC requirementsAbility to use and adapt to technology systems supporting fitness programs and servicesAbility to establish goals, manage competing priorities, meet deadlines, and respond to operational needsAbility to communicate effectively, verbally and in writing, and prepare clear, accurate reports and documentationAbility to provide excellent customer service and resolve escalated concernsAbility to collaborate and maintain effective working relationships with staff, campus partners, vendors, and community membersDemonstrated commitment to valuing justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion, and contributing to an inclusive working and learning environmentAbility to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and handle sensitive matters professionallyAbility to work independently under general supervision and collaboratively as part of a team WORKING CONDITIONS:Work is generally performed in a temperature-controlled office, fitness, recreation, and outdoor environments, occasionally in extreme weather conditions. Depending on the time of year, average outdoor temperatures may range from 50 degrees in winter to over 100 degrees in summer. The position requires the ability to work under pressure, respond to changing operational needs, and adhere to deadlines. SUPERVISION EXERCISED:This position directly supervises one (1) full-time Coordinator, Fitness Training, one (1) part-time student assistant employee, approximately ten (10) part-time, non-student Group Exercise Instructors and indirectly supervises approximately six (6) part-time student assistant employees and approximately nine (9) part-time, non-student Personal Trainers. PAY, BENEFITS AND WORK SCHEDULE:This position is employed through University Student Union (USU). The USU offers an excellent benefits package including Medical, Dental & Vision insurance, Life Insurance, Vacation, Sick Leave, 14 paid Holidays, company-sponsored retirement program, and more. The anticipated hiring range will be as follows and is dependent on experience and qualifications:Hourly: Minimum: $36.06 Maximum: $38.46Bi-Weekly: Minimum: $2,884.62 Maximum: $3,076.92Annually: Minimum: $75,000.00 Maximum: $80,000.00The salary range of the position is as follows:Hourly: Minimum: $31.96 Maximum: $45.54Bi-Weekly: Minimum: $2,556.92 Maximum: $3,642.92Annually: Minimum: $66,480.00 Maximum: $94,716.00 APPLICATION PERIOD:Applications received through December 8, 2026 will be considered in the initial review. Review of applications will begin after this date and continue until the position is filled.In order to be considered in the initial review, applications must be submitted prior to the date listed above. Application submissions received after the initial review date will be reviewed at the discretion of the USU. HOW TO APPLY:Candidates should apply by completing the online application. To submit an application and for more detailed information on the application and hiring process, please visit this link: www.csun.edu/careers BACKGROUND CHECK:A background check (including a criminal records check) must be completed satisfactorily. Failure to satisfactorily complete the background check may affect the status of candidates who apply for the position. CANRA:The person holding this position is considered a 'mandated reporter' under the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and is required to comply with the requirements set forth in CSU Executive Order 1083 as a condition of employment.

jobs.title: IT Multimedia Production Student Assistant at CSUN 10052 - Information Technology
jobs.description: Employer: CSUN 10052 - Information Technology Expires: 12/20/2026 Student Job Title: IT – Academic Technology Multimedia Production Student Assistant Contact: Tim Aguirre (timothy.aguirre@csun.edu) Office: Oviatt – Room 34Starting Rate: $17.00Hours: 20 hours/week Position Reports To:Marketing and Media Services LeadPurpose:Academic Technology (AT) is part of the Division of Information Technology (IT). The AT Multimedia Production area provides technical assistance to campus partners. These partners might include colleges, departments, CSUN organizations or clubs, individual faculty, student projects, or other on-campus productions.About this Position: The student assistant will provide technical support to faculty and students through in-person interactions. Responsibilities may include creating multimedia instructional materials and assisting with pre-production, production, and post-production duties as needed to support campus partners. This may include on-campus recordings and livestreams, supporting presentations, and special events. The ideal candidate will demonstrate strong technical skills, effective interpersonal communication, creativity, dependability, and the ability to prioritize tasks, complete projects on time, and identify opportunities for improvement. This is primarily an in-person position requiring regular on-campus availability, with occasional opportunities for remote work when appropriate.Qualifications: Needs to be highly computer- and internet-literate. Must be familiar with using Adobe Creative Suite (especially Adobe Premiere and After Effects, though knowledge of additional CC applications is a plus), Camtasia, Microsoft Office, Mac/Windows operating systems, video and photography equipment (cameras, lights, audio recorders, microphones). Knowledge of web and graphic design is a plus. Willing to learn new tools for multimedia production in relatively short order. Must be able to work accurately and efficiently, both independently and in collaboration with others. Must be able to lift video equipment and office furniture. Students from all academic disciplines are encouraged to apply. We welcome applicants who are enthusiastic about technology and production, enjoy helping others, and are eager to develop new technical and creative skills. Areas of Responsibility and Description of Duties:1. Video production1.1. Participate in the set-up and take-down of equipment needed for video production.1.2. Act as a primary or additional camera operator on studio, location, and live broadcast productions as needed.1.3. Assist with lighting, cinematography, and audio-recording of video projects.1.4. Assist in pre-production preparation and location scouting.1.5. Gather and file release forms on shoots, as needed.1.6. Back up raw footage to a laptop or external hard drives, as needed.1.7. Capture and edit video content using Camtasia. 2. Video post-production and captioning2.1. Perform or assist in video editing and post-production on multimedia projects (including videos, slideshows, and slide presentations), using Adobe Premiere, Adobe After Effects, DaVinci Resolve, or other software as assigned.2.2. Ingest raw footage into laptop or desktop editing systems and convert to other formats using Adobe Media Encoder.2.3. Design or manipulate templates for visual effects and motion graphics using Adobe After Effects.2.4. Generate captions and transcripts for accessible videos using Premiere Pro for transcripts and captioning or other software as assigned.2.5. Manage project data by keeping or deleting digital files as directed. 3. Delivery and distribution of video content 3.1. Perform or assist in converting DVD and VHS using MakeMKV and Handbrake.3.2. Convert videos to h.264 and upload to Panopto, YouTube, or other streaming platforms.3.3. Deliver video content using OneDrive. 3.4. Embed videos in Keynote or PowerPoint for presentations. 3.5. Convert video and audio content to other formats as needed. 4. Photography and graphics editing4.1. Take photographs as a primary or additional still camera operator as needed.4.2. Edit photographs in Adobe Photoshop. 4.3. Manipulate and resize photographs, illustrations, or other graphics/images and insert these files into presentations, etexts, or websites. 5. Other 5.1. Assist or help train faculty to perform any of the above multimedia tasks.5.2. Assist in Faculty Technology Center client support as needed5.3. Help move tables, chairs, or other furniture and equipment (during set-up for a video production, training session, conference, meeting, or other event).5.4. Other duties as assigned. Working Relationships: Reports to the Marketing and Media Services Lead. Have continuous interaction with IT team members, including staff and student assistants. Interacts with and assists university faculty and staff on IT-supported projects and services. Job Location/Working Conditions: Primarily works in the Faculty Technology Center - University Library, Garden Level, Room 35 and neighboring rooms. Office space is shared with other student assistants. Employment Duration:Renewable annually

jobs.title: Research Assistant at CSUN 24200 - Autonomy Research Center for STEAHM
jobs.description: Employer: CSUN 24200 - Autonomy Research Center for STEAHM Expires: 12/02/2026 Research Assistant — Convergence Research, Innovation, and Societal Impact Book ProjectPosition: Undergraduate or Graduate Research AssistantFaculty Lead: Dr. Nhut Tan HoSenior Advisor: Dr. Peter GrayProject: Convergence in Action: How Deep Integration Across Disciplines and Sectors Turns Complex Problems into Innovation and Societal ImpactHours: Approximately 10 hours/week, depending on assignmentCompensation and duration: $18/hour and academic year, with possibility of continuation Project DescriptionStudents are invited to participate in the research and development of a book examining how universities, government, industry, and other organizations work across disciplinary and institutional boundaries to address complex societal and technological problems.The book will draw on case studies from the National Science Foundation's convergence research programs, selected MIT and other universities’ initiatives, and the NASA-sponsored Autonomy Research Center for STEAHM (ARCS) at CSUN. It will investigate not only what these projects accomplished, but how successful convergence efforts are designed and operated.Major questions include:What distinguishes genuine convergence from conventional interdisciplinary research?How are effective cross-disciplinary and cross-sector teams created?How are complex societal problems identified and framed?How do teams integrate different disciplines, methods, and perspectives?How do government, industry, communities, and end users participate?What organizational barriers prevent convergence?How does research move toward innovation and societal impact?What institutional practices make convergence sustainable?Student Responsibilities:Depending on interests and background, research assistants may participate in one or more of the following:research NSF-funded convergence projects and investigators;collect and verify project information from authoritative sources;search scholarly literature, reports, project websites, publications, patents, and other evidence of outcomes;develop structured case-study research dossiers;analyze how multidisciplinary teams were formed and operated;identify evidence of research translation and societal impact;conduct background research on interview subjects;assist in preparing interview questions;organize and analyze interview transcripts;code interviews and cases for recurring themes and lessons learned;maintain bibliographic records and research databases;research MIT and other institutional convergence models;document lessons from ARCS projects and participants;prepare concise research summaries, tables, timelines, and visual materials;support fact-checking, references, and manuscript development.Students will not simply summarize sources. They will be trained to analyze each case using a common framework:Problem → Team → Integration → Stakeholders → Translation → Outcomes → LessonsDesired QualificationsStrong candidates will have:intellectual curiosity and interest in research, innovation, technology, or societal problems;strong reading and analytical skills;careful attention to evidence and accuracy;ability to summarize complex material clearly;reliability and ability to work independently;strong written English;comfort learning topics outside their primary discipline.Students from all disciplines are encouraged to apply, including engineering, computer science, social sciences, humanities, business, health sciences, communication, design, and education.Prior research experience is helpful but not required.Particularly Valuable SkillsExperience with any of the following is useful:literature searches;qualitative research;interview analysis;data organization;Zotero or other reference-management software;Excel/Google Sheets;bibliographic databases;visualization;AI-assisted research tools used responsibly;technical or science writing.What Students Will LearnStudents will gain experience in:convergence and interdisciplinary research;science and innovation policy;qualitative and case-study research;scholarly literature review;analysis of large research programs;interviewing and qualitative coding;research translation and societal-impact assessment;working directly with faculty and national research leaders.Students may also have opportunities to participate in conversations with researchers, government program leaders, university leaders, and other experts involved in major convergence initiatives.ApplicationInterested students should submit their application package below to this link https://forms.gle/6GaGcmpLwyqb28F48 :a brief statement of interest (approximately 250 words);résumé/CV;academic major and year;description of any relevant research, writing, data, or analytical experience;one example of a complex problem or project that interests you and why you think multiple disciplines would be needed to address it.
